claim.summary: For fixed prime p, input circuits F_i over F_p of total size s/depth Delta, and Boolean B_j=x_j^2-x_j, put A=product_i(1-F_i^(p-1)). A general IPS certificate of size S/depth d yields a circuit Q(x,Z), linear in Z, with Q(x,0)=0 and Q(x,B)=A, at polynomial size in S+s+n+m and depth O(d+Delta+1). Conversely Q yields a full certificate with input coefficients F_i^(p-2) product_(l<i)(1-F_l^(p-1)). The forward proof explicitly linearizes general IPS by gate telescoping and constructs small Frobenius Boolean-defect certificates. No PC-degree, multilinearity-in-x or extension-field preservation is claimed.

claim.summary: Over any field, let literal CNF violation products F_i and all Boolean B_j=x_j^2-x_j have Hilbert-like certificate C(x,Y,Z), size S depth d. Put P=product_i(1-F_i), P_i=product_(k!=i)(1-F_k), and literal-telescoping T_i(x,B)=F_i^2-F_i. Then Q=C(x,(-P_i T_i(x,Z))_i,(P Z_j)_j) satisfies Q(x,B)=P, is Hilbert-like and has size O(S+s^3), depth<=d+10, s=m+n+literal length+1, counting gates and wires with unbounded fan-in. Conversely sum_i(product_(k<i)(1-F_k))Y_i+Q gives a certificate with fixed clause coefficients, size O(S+s^3), depth<=max(d,6)+2. Repeated, tautological and empty clauses allowed; polynomial Hilbert-likeness suffices.

claim.summary: There is no generic polynomial-size fixed-depth operation extracting arbitrary homogeneous components from all polynomial-size fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuits of polynomial degree. Already G_n=product(1+x_i), q=2^a, n=2q-1 has degree-q component e_q evaluating to majority, since binomial(w,q) mod2 is the a-th bit of w. Such an operation would contradict Smolensky's majority lower bound for AC0[2]. Binary constants and unbounded-fanin gates with wire size are essential.
claim.assessment: Working attributed elementary consequence of the published majority lower bound, medium reviewed. Does not rule out special component extraction with additional hypotheses or large-field interpolation.
